correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary positive-definite quadratic pullback, averaging over the coordinate sign symmetries preserves the full lower and upper comparison constants and produces a diagonal form with no worse distortion. On the unit sphere a diagonal form becomes F_{a,b}(t)=a t^(2/p)+b(1-t)^(2/q). Since both exponents lie strictly between 0 and 1, this profile is strictly concave and has endpoint minimum min(a,b). After normalizing that minimum to 1, a,b>=1, so F_{a,b}>=F_{1,1} pointwise; at the interior maximizer of F_{1,1}, the inequality is strict unless a=b=1, proving unique diagonal optimality up to scale. Strict concavity gives a unique interior maximizer. If an arbitrary optimal form had a nonzero cross term, opposite sign choices at the maximizing absolute-value pair would raise the maximum above the optimum while axis values keep the minimum at most 1. Hence the cross term vanishes and the circle is unique up to scale.

value.rationale: The coordinatewise mixed-power plane is the basic two-dimensional non-permutation-symmetric Musielak-Orlicz model with two genuinely superquadratic exponents. Despite that anisotropy, the theorem shows that the Euclidean circle, not a tilted or axis-rescaled ellipse, is uniquely optimal and gives the exact two-parameter distortion through a single intrinsic contact equation. This is a natural benchmark for variable-exponent finite-dimensional geometry rather than an isolated parameter computation.
